P.w: The public building Apple built across the street from its 'spaceship' ring HQ, opened 2017. A design landmark in its own right, with a carbon-fiber roof floating on stone columns.
P.k: Open to anyone: full Apple Store, Caffe Macs rooftop cafe/terrace with a distant view over the ring, and an augmented-reality tabletop model of the campus. The ring building itself and the grounds are closed to the public.

P.n: Steve Jobs' Childhood Home & Apple Garage
P.w: The ranch house where Steve Jobs grew up and where he and Steve Wozniak built the first Apple I computers in the garage in 1976. Los Altos designated it a historic resource in 2013.
P.k: View from the public street ONLY. It is a private, occupied residence with no plaque or tour; do not enter the property or disturb residents. Just a quiet curbside pilgrimage.

P.ad: 2000 N Shoreline Blvd, Mountain View, CA 94043
P.w: Google's official public front door at the Googleplex, opened October 2023 inside the striking curved 'Gradient Canopy' (Charleston East) building. The rest of the Googleplex is closed to non-employees.
P.k: Open to the public: the Google Store (hardware + exclusive branded merch), a cafe, the Huddle event space and an outdoor Plaza with public art. Offices and the wider campus are off-limits.

P.ad: Charleston Rd & Huff Ave, Mountain View, CA 94043
P.w: The beloved oversized foam sculptures of Android dessert mascots (Cupcake through Pie, etc.). The tradition ran 2008-2019; newer versions are digital-only.
P.k: An outdoor photo spot beside the Google Visitor Experience. The statues were moved here from the old Landings Drive lawn (redeveloped) in 2022; the area is technically for Google employees and guests, but visitors are generally welcomed to walk up and photograph them. Best combined with a Visitor Experience stop.

P.ad: 1401 N Shoreline Blvd, Mountain View, CA 94043
P.w: The world's leading museum of computing history, holding everything from a working Babbage Difference Engine reconstruction to Cray supercomputers and a restored PDP-1. A must for any tech traveler.
P.k: Fully open to the public (Wed-Sun, ~10a-5p; general admission ~$15). No membership or affiliation needed.

P.ad: 2200 Mission College Blvd, Santa Clara, CA 95054
P.w: A free museum at Intel's HQ tracing the silicon-chip story from the transistor to modern processors, with hands-on exhibits on how chips are made and Intel's Silicon Valley founding.
P.k: Free and open to the public inside the Robert Noyce Building lobby (Mon-Fri, ~9a-5p; call ahead as it closes for events). The rest of the Intel campus is not public.

P.ad: 2788 San Tomas Expy, Santa Clara, CA 95051
P.w: NVIDIA's dramatic triangle-motif headquarters: the Gensler-designed Endeavor (2017) and the enormous Voyager (2022), whose sloped glass 'mountain' roof shelters an indoor landscaped village.
P.k: Exterior architecture only. The buildings are private and closed to the public; the striking hexagonal/triangular forms are best appreciated from the sidewalk and San Tomas Expressway. No visitor center or tours.

P.n: HP Garage - Birthplace of Silicon Valley
P.w: The one-car garage where Bill Hewlett and Dave Packard started Hewlett-Packard in 1939, widely honored as the birthplace of Silicon Valley. California Historical Landmark and on the National Register.
P.k: View from the public sidewalk ONLY. It is a private HP-owned property, not open inside; a bronze plaque on the front lawn reads 'Birthplace of Silicon Valley.'

P.ad: 3333 Coyote Hill Rd, Palo Alto, CA 94304
P.w: The low-slung research lab (now PARC, part of SRI International) where the graphical user interface, the mouse, Ethernet, laser printing and WYSIWYG editing were invented in the 1970s - ideas that shaped every modern computer.
P.k: Exterior/landmark only. It is a working private research facility, not open to the public; the site sits on Coyote Hill above Stanford with hiking-trail views nearby. A pilgrimage for the story, not the building.

P.n: NASA Ames Exploration Center & Hangar One
P.w: NASA's free space-science visitor center at Ames Research Center/Moffett Field, with Mercury and Apollo-era artifacts, a Mars meteorite and moon-mission exhibits. Nearby looms Hangar One, the colossal 1930s airship hangar that is a Bay Area landmark.
P.k: The Exploration Center sits outside the security gate and is free and open to the public (Tue-Fri 10a-4p, Sat-Sun 12-4p) - no base access needed. Hangar One and the airfield itself are secured; the hangar is viewable from outside/afar only. (The separate Moffett Field Museum, inside the gate, requires ID and a fee.)

P.w: The famous sign at the entrance to Meta's (Facebook's) headquarters - once the giant blue thumbs-up 'Like', now the blue Meta infinity logo (swapped in the 2021 rebrand). A classic Silicon Valley selfie stop.
P.k: Photo stop at the entrance sign ONLY, from the public roadside. The Meta campus is closed to the public - no walk-in access. The famous thumbs-up is gone; the sign now shows the Meta infinity mark (with 'Facebook' still on the reverse).

P.ad: 151 S Almaden Blvd, San Jose, CA 95113
P.w: Adobe's cluster of towers that anchors downtown San Jose's skyline. Atop the Almaden Tower is the 'San Jose Semaphore,' a public art installation of four rotating LED disks that broadcast an encoded message.
P.k: Exterior and skyline only - the offices are private. The San Jose Semaphore art piece is visible free from the street/downtown after dark (message decodable online). No public interior or tours.

P.w: The headquarters campus of eBay, one of the dot-com era's defining companies, whose whimsical signage and 'Main Street' welcome center reflect its marketplace roots.
P.k: Exterior and signage only. The campus is a private workplace not open to the public; the branded eBay sign and buildings can be seen from the roadside.

P.ad: 3655 N First St, San Jose, CA 95134
P.w: Samsung's striking 10-story North American semiconductor HQ (opened 2015), a LEED-Platinum tower with a sculptural stepped facade - the standout landmark of North San Jose's 'Golden Triangle' tech corridor along N First St, which also hosts PayPal, Cisco and others.
P.k: Exterior architecture and signage only. The building is a private office, not open to the public; admire the facade from N First St. Neighboring PayPal (2211 N First St) and Cisco (170 W Tasman Dr) campuses are likewise exteriors-only drive-bys.

P.w: A historic 2.5-acre estate garden in downtown Palo Alto, with formal rose and perennial beds, a wisteria arbor and the 1902 Gamble family house. A quiet horticultural retreat open daily during daylight hours.
P.k: Grounds free and open every day at daylight; the Main House and offices keep weekday hours (roughly 9am-2pm). Donations encouraged.

P.ad: 3300 Page Mill Rd, Los Altos Hills, CA 94022
P.w: A 1,400-acre Palo Alto nature preserve in the Santa Cruz Mountain foothills, with oak woodland trails, Boronda Lake and sweeping ridge views. Famous for being residents-only from 1969 until it finally opened to everyone in December 2020.
P.k: Now open to all; a small per-vehicle entry fee applies and the lot can fill on weekends. Open sunrise to sunset.

P.ad: 51 S San Antonio Rd, Los Altos, CA 94022
P.w: A free community museum telling the story of the Santa Clara Valley's orchard era and its turn into Silicon Valley, set on a campus beside the 1905 J. Gilbert Smith farmhouse. A gentle stop in downtown Los Altos.
P.k: Free admission; open Thursday-Sunday, roughly noon-4pm. Closed major holidays.
s: mv-voice.com — Heather Zimmerman review of the 'Making Connections: Stories from the Land' permanent exhibit
Los Altos Town Crier — coverage of Making Connections exhibit grand opening / Ikebana front-page feature

P.w: A beloved 32-acre Mountain View neighborhood park shaded by mature redwoods and oaks, with tennis courts, playgrounds, picnic lawns and a demonstration garden. A classic local weekend spot.
P.k: Free; parking off Cuesta Dr fills on sunny weekends. Better as a picnic/family stop than a destination sight.
s: Cuesta Park profile — https://www.mv-voice.com/real-estate/2017/06/14/cuesta-park/ ; also Best of Mountain View & Sliding through the Peninsula's playgrounds

P.w: The character-filled heart of downtown Sunnyvale: a block of restored late-1800s brick storefronts named for pioneer Martin Murphy Jr., now a pedestrian-only strip of restaurants, cafes and shops. Converted to a walking mall in 2023.
P.k: Free to stroll; liveliest at the Saturday farmers market and in the evenings. On-street/garage parking nearby.
s: https://www.paloaltoonline.com/ae/2026/02/19/downtown-sunnyvale-developments-where-to-play-dine-and-unwind-in-a-transforming-silicon-valley-corridor/ (names Murphy Avenue as heart of downtown Sunnyvale)

P.w: A 177-acre bayfront park on the edge of the salt marsh, with seasonal wetlands, a large playground, picnic areas and flat trails linking to the Bay Trail. A joint city-county park good for birding and kite-flying.
P.k: Per-vehicle parking fee on weekends and holidays; open 8am to 30 minutes after sunset. Windy near the marsh.
s: sanjosespotlight.com / x.com/SJSpotlight/status/1808525028113416563 — Baylands Park drone light show coverage

P.w: A small volunteer-run museum housed in a replica of the historic Murphy family's Bay View farmhouse, set in Orchard Heritage Park amid one of the valley's last surviving apricot orchards. Free local history exhibits.
P.k: Free; open limited hours (typically Tue/Thu/Sun afternoons). Combine with a walk through the adjacent heritage orchard.

P.w: A green Sunnyvale neighborhood park with a pond, big playground, tennis and a walking loop shaded by palms and redwoods. An easygoing family stop away from the tech campuses.
P.k: Free; mainly a picnic/playground park rather than a marquee sight.

P.w: The walkable historic core of Saratoga along Big Basin Way (once 1850s 'Lumber Street'), lined with wine-country-style restaurants, galleries, boutiques and Blaney Plaza. The gateway to Hakone Gardens and Montalvo.
P.k: Free to wander; parking on Big Basin Way and side lots. Best paired with a nearby garden or winery visit.
s: Saratoga cover: Big Basin Way, downtown Saratoga's main street becoming a destination — https://www.metrosiliconvalley.com/metro/10.24.07/cover-saratoga-0743.html

P.w: A rustic 18-acre former horse ranch preserved as a nature area on Stevens Creek, with 1930s barns, a blacksmith shop, community gardens, a rotary nature museum and an environmental education center. A designated Cupertino natural preserve.
P.k: Free; open daily 6am to dusk. Saturday open-house and last-Saturday blacksmith demos are the liveliest times.

P.w: A free art museum on El Camino Real focused on Bay Area and California artists, with rotating exhibitions, a permanent collection and a sculpture garden on the grounds. A well-kept Santa Clara secret.
P.k: Free admission and free parking; open Tuesday-Sunday, 11am-5pm, closed Mondays.

P.ad: 500 El Camino Real, Santa Clara, CA 95053
P.w: Santa Clara University's free art and history museum, holding a California/mission-era collection and rotating fine-art shows, next to the historic Mission Santa Clara on the leafy campus. Accredited and free to all.
P.k: Free; open Tuesday-Sunday afternoons, closed Mondays. Check the site as campus schedules shift hours.

P.w: A 4,163-acre park on the grounds of the New Almaden mercury ('quicksilver') mines, which ran for 135 years and helped fuel the Gold Rush. Over 37 miles of trails wind past mine ruins, brick chimneys and hillside views above south San Jose.
P.k: Free entry; hot and exposed in summer with little water. The nearby Casa Grande / New Almaden Quicksilver Mining Museum tells the mine story.

P.w: A neoclassical Beaux-Arts temple built by the SFPUC in 1934 to mark where Hetch Hetchy water — piped 160 miles from Yosemite — arrives on the Peninsula, framed by cypress and a long reflecting pool. A striking, little-known monument near Woodside.
P.k: Free; grounds open weekdays 9am-5pm, and to pedestrians/cyclists on weekends (the parking lot is closed weekends and holidays). Off Cañada Rd near I-280.

P.ad: 2531 W Cliff Dr, Santa Cruz, CA 95060
P.w: A pretty Santa Cruz cove named for its remaining natural rock arch, with tide pools and, from mid-October to mid-February, California's only State Monarch Butterfly Preserve, where thousands of monarchs cluster in the eucalyptus grove.
P.k: Open 8am to sunset; parking about $10. Monarchs are seasonal (roughly November-January is peak) — the beach is worth it year-round.

P.ad: 701 W Cliff Dr, Santa Cruz, CA 95060
P.w: A scenic ~3-mile clifftop walking and biking path running from the wharf to Natural Bridges, overlooking Monterey Bay and the world-famous Steamer Lane surf break. Lighthouse Point holds the tiny Santa Cruz Surfing Museum.
P.k: Free and always open; storm damage has closed short stretches to cars in recent years, but the coastal path remains the draw. Parking along the bluff.

P.ad: 465 Mystery Spot Rd, Santa Cruz, CA 95065
P.w: A classic 1940s roadside gravity-illusion attraction in the redwoods above Santa Cruz, where a tilted cabin makes balls appear to roll uphill and people seem to change height. A campy, only-in-California guided tour.
P.k: Paid timed tours every half hour (~$12), plus $5 cash parking; it sells out midday. Arrive 30 minutes early. Open daily.

P.w: A coastal state park just north of Santa Cruz combining a preserved 1800s dairy ranch (Victorian farmhouse, adobe, working blacksmith) with bluff-top trails over pocket beaches and tide pools. Popular with hikers and mountain bikers.
P.k: Day-use parking about $10 (free on foot or bike); park open 8am-sunset, the historic Interpretive Center Thursday-Sunday.

P.w: A 19th-century-style logging camp in Felton running two heritage trains: an 1890s narrow-gauge steam train that climbs through old-growth redwoods to Bear Mountain, and a diesel line down the San Lorenzo gorge to the Santa Cruz Boardwalk.
P.k: Paid excursions; gates open 9am-5pm on operating days. Book steam-train tickets ahead, especially for holiday and Thomas events.

P.w: One of the tallest lighthouses in the U.S. — a 115-foot 1872 tower on a dramatic bluff on the San Mateo coast, 5 miles south of Pescadero. A photogenic Highway 1 landmark now run as a state historic park (and hostel).
P.k: Grounds free and open daily for photos and whale-watching; the tower itself has long been closed for restoration, so views are from the base. Bring a windbreaker.

P.ad: Mount Umunhum Rd, Los Gatos, CA 95033
P.w: A 3,486-foot Santa Cruz Mountains peak inside Sierra Azul Open Space Preserve, crowned by 'the Cube' — the concrete base of a Cold War radar tower from the former Almaden Air Force Station. Reopened to the public in 2017 with 360-degree Bay-to-ocean views.
P.k: Free; reach the summit by the paved Mount Umunhum Rd or a strenuous ~3.7-mile trail from the Bald Mountain lot. The narrow mountain road can close in bad weather — check before going.

P.ad: 1 Johnson Pier, Half Moon Bay, CA 94019
P.w: A working fishing harbor at Princeton-by-the-Sea and the launch point for Mavericks, the legendary big-wave surf break a half-mile offshore where winter swells top 60 feet. Harbor tide pools, seafood shacks and coastal trails round out a day.
P.k: Harbor free to visit; to glimpse Mavericks, park at the Pillar Point bluff lot and walk the dirt trail. Big-wave season is roughly November-March.

P.w: California's newest national park (2013): the eroded remnants of an ancient volcano, with jagged rock spires, talus caves and one of the best places in the state to spot free-flying California condors. A striking, harder-to-reach day trip southeast of Gilroy.
P.k: About 1.5-2 hours from San Jose; the east and west entrances are NOT connected by road. Entry fee per vehicle; brutally hot in summer, best in spring. High Peaks Trail is the top condor spot.

P.ad: Stanford Ave & Junipero Serra Blvd, Stanford, CA 94305
P.w: An iconic ~3.7-mile paved loop over Stanford's rolling foothills, named for the giant radio telescope dish on the ridge, with sweeping views of the Bay and campus. A local exercise ritual dawn to dusk.
P.k: No dogs, no bikes; free street parking on Stanford Ave fills early on weekends. No water on the loop.

P.w: One of the largest tracts of undisturbed marshland left on the Bay, with 15 miles of flat trails, boardwalks and superb birding along the salt marsh and sloughs. The Lucy Evans Interpretive Center sits at 2775 Embarcadero Rd.
P.k: Flat and stroller/bike friendly; best light and bird activity at sunrise and sunset.

P.ad: 3160 N Shoreline Blvd, Mountain View, CA 94043
P.w: A 750-acre bayfront park built on former landfill, with a 50-acre sailing lake, kite-flying meadows, burrowing owls and miles of paved trails linking to the Bay Trail. The historic Rengstorff House stands near the entrance.
P.k: Boat and kayak rentals at the lake; Shoreline Amphitheatre concerts can jam parking on show nights.

P.w: The South Bay's most popular open space: 24 miles of oak-and-grassland trails, the family-favorite Deer Hollow Farm, and the climb to Wildcat Loop and PG&E Trail. Open 8 a.m. to 30 minutes after sunset.
P.k: The lot fills by mid-morning on weekends; arrive early or expect to wait.

P.w: A 739-acre preserve of hayfields, oak woodland and orchard on the Saratoga/Cupertino line, with two lookout peaks (Hunters Point, Maisie's Peak) giving valley-wide views. A favorite of hikers, riders and mountain bikers.
P.k: Only ~21 spaces at the Prospect Rd lot; go early. Trails are shared with bikes and horses.

P.w: Santa Clara County's first regional park (1924): 1,077 acres of foothills around a 92-acre reservoir, with hiking, fishing, non-motorized boating and links to the Fremont Older and Skyline trails.
P.k: $6 parking at the ranger station; a second lot near the reservoir is closer to the water.

P.w: One of the oldest Japanese-style residential gardens in the Western Hemisphere (est. 1917), with a koi pond, tea house, bamboo grove and hillside strolling paths. A National Historic District in the Saratoga hills.
P.k: Paid admission; the Lower House and tea garden are best in spring azalea and fall maple season.

P.w: A serene 6.5-acre koi garden in Kelley Park modeled on Okayama's Korakuen, sister city to San Jose, with waterfalls, arched bridges and hundreds of koi. Free to enter.
P.k: Inside Kelley Park; parking on Senter Rd. Combine with the neighboring Happy Hollow zoo.

P.ad: Naglee Ave & Dana Ave, San Jose, CA 95126
P.w: A 5.5-acre historic rose garden with roughly 3,500 plantings of nearly 200 varieties, repeatedly voted America's Best Rose Garden. Peak bloom is late April through the summer.
P.k: Free; on-street parking. Fragrance and color peak in May. GPS 1649 Naglee Ave.

P.ad: 368 Educational Park Dr, San Jose, CA 95133
P.w: A quiet 33-acre passive park with ponds, a fragrance/sensory garden and the Chinese Cultural Garden, complete with a Friendship Gate and a towering statue of Confucius. Free and rarely crowded.
P.k: Free entry; wandering pathways suit a slow stroll rather than a workout.

P.ad: 15350 Penitencia Creek Rd, San Jose, CA 95127
P.w: Founded in 1872, one of California's oldest municipal parks: 720 acres of rugged canyon in the Diablo foothills, with mineral springs, stone grottoes, a creek and 13 miles of trails. Open 8 a.m. to a half-hour after sunset.
P.k: Weekend parking fee; the Creek and North Rim trails give the best canyon views.

P.w: The Bay Area's most famous foothill summit hike: a relentless ~6-mile round trip climbing 2,000 ft to a 2,517-ft peak and its selfie-famous survey pole, with 360-degree valley and Bay views. A rite of passage for South Bay hikers.
P.k: Tiny Stanford Ave lot fills at dawn; overflow on Vineyard Ave. Bring water, no shade. Entrance open 6:30 a.m.

P.ad: 7281 Mt Hamilton Rd, Mount Hamilton, CA 95140
P.w: A working University of California observatory on the 4,200-ft summit of Mt Hamilton, reached by a famously winding road with knockout views over San Jose. Free visitor center and tours of the historic 36-inch Great Refractor.
P.k: Public grounds open weekends noon-5 p.m.; the drive is long and twisty with no gas or food. Check for construction closures.

P.w: A 1917 Georgian country estate on 654 acres in Woodside, with 16 acres of formal English Renaissance gardens, reflecting pools and seasonal displays. A National Trust site open daily 10 a.m.-5 p.m.
P.k: Paid, often timed-ticket admission; spring tulips and the holiday displays draw crowds. Book ahead.

P.ad: 21600 Big Basin Way, Boulder Creek, CA 95006
P.w: California's oldest state park (1902) and its old-growth coast redwoods. Badly burned in the 2020 CZU fire, it has reopened for limited day-use with reservations; over 20 miles of trails are restored and the forest is visibly regenerating.
P.k: Day-use reservations required; a summer weekend/holiday shuttle runs. Full rebuild will take years, so check current access before going.

P.ad: 101 Big Trees Park Rd, Felton, CA 95018
P.w: An accessible grove of ancient coast redwoods near Felton, with an easy self-guided Redwood Loop, the San Lorenzo River and trails up to an observation deck. A gentler redwood day than Big Basin.
P.k: Day-use fee; the flat Redwood Loop is stroller-friendly. The Roaring Camp steam railroad runs nearby.

P.w: California's classic beachfront amusement park, home to the 1924 wooden Giant Dipper coaster and the 1911 Looff carousel, both National Historic Landmarks. Free to enter, pay per ride; open year-round.
P.k: Free admission, ride wristbands sold separately; summer weekends are packed and parking is tight.

P.ad: 95 Kelly Ave, Half Moon Bay, CA 94019
P.w: Four miles of sandy state beach on the San Mateo coast, edged by the level, paved Coastside Trail running from Pillar Point to Poplar Beach with wide-open ocean views. Day-use 8 a.m. to sunset.
P.k: Francis Beach is at the end of Kelly Ave; the coast is windy and cold-water, more for walking than swimming.

P.w: A horticulture-themed family park in the garlic capital of Gilroy, built around famous 'circus trees' and six gardens with gentle rides and attractions. Seasonal, open roughly late March through early January.
P.k: Paid admission; low-key rides aimed at younger kids. Pair with Gilroy's garlic scene and the July Garlic Festival heritage.

P.ad: 4900 Marie P DeBartolo Way, Santa Clara, CA 95054
P.w: Home of the NFL's San Francisco 49ers and host of Super Bowl 50 and the 2026 Super Bowl LX, this open-air stadium also holds the 49ers Museum, an 20,000-sq-ft hall of trophies, memorabilia, and Hall of Fame exhibits.
P.k: Stadium interior only by game/event ticket or scheduled tour. The 49ers Museum keeps separate hours (typically Fri-Sun) on non-event days; on gamedays it needs both a game and a museum ticket. Verify hours before visiting.

P.n: SAP Center at San Jose (The Shark Tank)
P.ad: 525 W Santa Clara St, San Jose, CA 95113
P.w: The 17,500-seat downtown arena nicknamed 'The Shark Tank,' home of the NHL's San Jose Sharks since 1993 and one of the busiest concert and event arenas in the country.
P.k: Interior accessible only with a ticket to a Sharks game, concert, or event. No general tours.

P.w: An 18,000-seat soccer-specific stadium beside the airport, home to MLS's San Jose Earthquakes and NWSL's Bay FC, known for its steep stands and the largest outdoor bar in North America.
P.k: Match-day or event ticket required to enter; no regular public access otherwise.

P.w: Northern California's largest outdoor amphitheater, opened in 1986 by Bill Graham, seating about 22,500 between reserved seats and a big grass lawn, next to Shoreline Park by the bay.
P.k: Open only for concerts, roughly May through October; entry by event ticket. Lawn seating is general admission.

P.w: A historic hilltop winery estate in the Saratoga foothills whose open-air amphitheater seats about 2,500 for an intimate summer concert series with sweeping views over Silicon Valley.
P.k: Concert season runs spring through fall; entry by event ticket. Gates open ~2 hours before showtime; ~$20 per car parking.

P.ad: 4701 Great America Pkwy, Santa Clara, CA 95054
P.w: A 100-acre amusement park opened in 1976 with roller coasters, a Boardwalk water area, and the landmark Carousel Columbia, celebrating its 50th season in 2026.
P.k: Seasonal ride park; entry by ticket. Slated to close after the 2027 season (lease expires 2028) unless extended - still fully operating for now.

P.ad: 400 S First St, San Jose, CA 95113
P.w: A 500-capacity live-music venue and nightclub in a former 1940s movie theater at the heart of the SoFA District, hosting touring rock, hip-hop, Latin, and electronic acts.
P.k: Open for scheduled shows and club nights only; entry by ticket. Check the calendar before going.

P.w: Silicon Valley's premier open-air shopping and dining district on Stevens Creek Blvd, a European-styled neighborhood of ~50 shops, 30-plus restaurants, a boutique hotel, and a cinema, dubbed the 'Rodeo Drive of Silicon Valley.'
P.k: Open-air district, free to stroll; individual shops and restaurants keep their own hours. Paid garages and street parking.

P.ad: 660 Stanford Shopping Center, Palo Alto, CA 94304
P.w: An upscale open-air mall on El Camino Real at Sand Hill Road with 140-plus specialty stores from luxury brands to local favorites, adjoining the Stanford campus.
P.k: Free to enter; store hours vary. Ample free parking.

P.w: The walkable spine of downtown Palo Alto, lined with boutiques, bookstores, cafes, art galleries, a cinema, and a dense run of restaurants a short walk from the Caltrain station.
P.k: Public street district, free to explore; shops and restaurants set their own hours. Street parking is tight at peak times; use the public garages.

P.w: Downtown Mountain View's pedestrian-friendly main street between Evelyn Ave and El Camino Real, packed with diverse restaurants, sidewalk cafes, beer gardens, boutiques, and a Sunday farmers' market.
P.k: Public street district (100-300 blocks are a pedestrian mall); free to walk. Individual businesses keep their own hours.

P.ad: N Santa Cruz Ave, Los Gatos, CA 95030
P.w: A picturesque four-to-five-block historic downtown along Santa Cruz Avenue with independent boutiques, art and cooking shops, fine dining, and turn-of-the-century architecture at the foot of the Santa Cruz Mountains.
P.k: Public street district, free to stroll; shop and restaurant hours vary. A pleasant day-trip stop en route to Santa Cruz.

P.w: A relaxed open-air shopping, dining, and cinema center at Bascom and Campbell Avenues, named for the prune orchards it replaced and known for the landmark 1980s free-speech Supreme Court case that bears its name.
P.k: Free to enter; store and restaurant hours vary. Just southwest of San Jose in Campbell.

P.ad: 387 S First St, San Jose, CA 95113
P.w: Downtown San Jose's 'Creative District' (South of First Area), a cluster of galleries, theaters, live-music clubs, and the SoFA Market food hall, anchored by the monthly South First Fridays art walk.
P.k: Public district, free to wander; the food hall and venues keep their own hours. South First Fridays runs the first Friday evening of each month.

P.ad: N 5th St & Jackson St, San Jose, CA 95112
P.w: One of only three surviving historic Japantowns in the U.S., centered on Jackson and Fifth Streets, with the Japanese American Museum, family-run shops and restaurants, temples, and Empire Seven Studios murals.
P.k: Public historic neighborhood, free to explore; museum, shops, and eateries keep their own hours. Also a strong food destination.

P.n: Children's Discovery Museum of San Jose
P.w: A large purple hands-on children's museum on Woz Way (named for Apple's Steve Wozniak, its biggest founding donor), with interactive exhibits on water, art, science, and community for young families.
P.k: Ticketed admission; check open days and hours before visiting. Near the convention center in downtown San Jose.

P.w: A family amusement park and accredited zoo in Kelley Park, mixing gentle rides, a puppet theater, and a Danny the Dragon ride with animal habitats for lemurs, jaguars, and more.
P.k: Ticketed admission; typically closed some weekdays - check the calendar. Parking at 748 Story Rd or 1300 Senter Rd.

P.n: Downtown San Jose Murals & Public Art
P.ad: 396 S First St, San Jose, CA 95113
P.w: An outdoor gallery of 70-plus murals and installations produced by Empire Seven Studios and the SJ Walls festival, concentrated in the SoFA District and Japantown, including El Mac's 'Sophie Holding the World Together' at Discovery Meadow.
P.k: Free, self-guided, viewable any time on public streets and walls. Cluster around S First St in SoFA; more in Japantown.

P.ad: N 2nd St & E St James St, San Jose, CA 95112
P.w: A 6.8-acre downtown square laid out in 1848, ringed by the St. James Square Historic District's landmark courthouse, post office, and churches, and the site where President McKinley once spoke.
P.k: Free public park, open daytime; a recent renovation has reopened it as a downtown green. Ringed by historic civic buildings.

P.ad: 110 S Market St, San Jose, CA 95113
P.w: Downtown's flagship art museum, set in a landmarked 1892 Richardsonian-Romanesque former post office joined to a modern wing, with a strong collection of modern and contemporary West Coast art.
P.k: Closed Mondays; open Tue-Sun (Fri until 9pm). Paid admission.

P.n: MACLA (Movimiento de Arte y Cultura Latino Americana)
P.w: A contemporary arts space in the SoFA District grounded in the Chicano/Latino experience, showing visual art, performance, and spoken word with free admission.
P.k: Gallery open Wed-Sun, roughly noon-5pm; free.

P.n: San Jose Museum of Quilts & Textiles
P.w: The first US museum devoted entirely to quilts and textiles, with rotating exhibitions of fiber art in the heart of the SoFA arts district.
P.k: Open Thu-Sun; closed early week. Paid admission.

P.n: Institute of Contemporary Art San Jose
P.w: A non-collecting contemporary art center in SoFA showing rotating exhibitions by emerging and established artists, with free admission and an active public-programs schedule.
P.k: Open Thu-Sun, noon-5pm; free.

P.n: Peralta Adobe & Fallon House Historic Site
P.ad: 175 W St John St, San Jose, CA 95110
P.w: Two eras side by side: the 1797 Peralta Adobe, the oldest surviving structure in San Jose and last remnant of the original Pueblo de San Jose, faces the ornate 1855 Fallon House built by an early city mayor.
P.k: Interiors are seen by guided tour only, generally weekend afternoons, booked in advance; the site is run by History San Jose. The surrounding street was renamed Sharks Way near the arena.

P.n: Japanese American Museum of San Jose
P.w: In the heart of San Jose's Japantown, this museum collects and preserves Japanese American history and culture, including the WWII incarceration era, with a focus on the Bay Area.
P.k: Open Thu-Sun, noon-4pm; closed Mon-Wed.

P.n: Viet Museum (Museum of the Boat People & the Republic of Vietnam)
P.w: Housed in the historic Greenwalt House within History Park at Kelley Park, this is believed to be the only museum focused on the Vietnamese diaspora and the boat-people exodus, in a city with one of the largest Vietnamese populations in the US.
P.k: Limited hours (often weekends); confirm before visiting. Inside History Park at Kelley Park.

P.ad: 647 S King Rd, San Jose, CA 95116
P.w: A 47-acre working farm park preserving San Jose's agricultural past, with the city's largest barn, a rare-fruit orchard, community gardens, and roaming farm animals, all free to visit.
P.k: Open daily 8:30am to sunset; free.

P.ad: 399 W Taylor St, San Jose, CA 95110
P.w: One of the largest public collections of rare and historic roses in the world, with roughly 3,000 varieties on nearly four acres of the Guadalupe River Park's Guadalupe Gardens.
P.k: Open daily sunrise to sunset; free. Best bloom in spring.

P.ad: 170 S Market St, San Jose, CA 95113
P.w: A 2.2-acre downtown park with a central fountain, ringed by the art museum, The Tech, and the adjacent Circle of Palms; on the site of the 1797 pueblo plaza, it is among the oldest public spaces in Northern California.
P.k: Open daily; free. Hosts frequent festivals and Music in the Park.

P.ad: 1700 Alum Rock Ave, San Jose, CA 95116
P.w: A landmark cultural campus on the Eastside, opened in 1999 and run by the School of Arts and Culture, with a 500-seat theater, galleries, gardens, and a pavilion celebrating Latino arts and heritage.
P.k: Grounds and gardens are open to the public; indoor venues are event- and program-driven, so check the calendar.

P.ad: 1375 E Santa Clara St, San Jose, CA 95116
P.w: The soaring Manueline-Gothic landmark of San Jose's Little Portugal, built 1916-19 partly from timbers salvaged from the Portuguese Pavilion of the 1915 Panama-Pacific Exposition.
P.k: An active parish; visit respectfully and check Mass times before entering.

P.w: The South First Area, downtown's compact arts-and-nightlife quarter along South First Street, packing MACLA, the ICA, the Quilts & Textiles museum, Anno Domini gallery, the historic California Theatre, and live-music venues into a few walkable blocks.
P.k: A walkable district (representative address given). Liveliest on the free South First Fridays art walk, first Friday each month.

P.ad: Jackson St & N 5th St, San Jose, CA 95112
P.w: One of only three surviving Japantowns in the United States and widely called the most authentic, this three-block Jackson Street district of family shops, markets, and restaurants dates to around 1900 and was named a California Cultural District in 2025.
P.k: A walkable neighborhood (central intersection given). Pair with the Japanese American Museum on N 5th St.

P.w: A tree-lined, small-town-feeling shopping and dining strip along Lincoln Avenue, with hundreds of independent boutiques, cafes, and restaurants a few miles southwest of downtown.
P.k: A walkable district (central address given); pedestrian-friendly, best on foot.

P.n: Don Edwards San Francisco Bay National Wildlife Refuge - Environmental Education Center
P.w: The southern gateway to the first urban national wildlife refuge in the US, on the restored salt-pond wetlands at Alviso, with an education center, boardwalks, and miles of level trails prized for birdwatching.
P.k: Trails open daily; the Environmental Education Center building keeps limited days/hours, so check ahead. Free.

P.w: Stanford's free art museum, whose 24-hour outdoor Rodin Sculpture Garden holds some 20 monumental bronzes, one of the largest Rodin collections outside Paris, alongside wide-ranging galleries indoors.
P.k: Museum closed Tue-Wed; free. The Rodin Sculpture Garden is open outdoors 24/7, free.

P.w: A purpose-built museum next to the Cantor housing the Anderson family's gift of postwar American painting, with major works by Pollock, Rothko, de Kooning, and Diebenkorn, all free to see.
P.k: Open Thu-Mon (closed Tue-Wed); free, no reservation needed.

P.w: The 285-foot 1941 landmark tower at the center of Stanford's campus, home to the Hoover Institution's library and archives, with an observation deck that gives sweeping views over the Peninsula.
P.k: The observation deck runs seasonal hours and closes for stretches (closed Aug 2026-Jan 2027); paid ticket to ascend. Verify it is open before visiting.

P.w: A hands-on children's science museum paired with a small zoo of rescued and native animals, rebuilt and reopened in 2021 as a bright, interactive family destination.
P.k: Closed Mondays; open Tue-Sun 10am-5pm.

P.w: Palo Alto's beloved community donkeys graze a pasture beside the Bol Park bike path; one resident, Perry, was a live model for the Donkey character in Shrek.
P.k: View free from the fence any time; volunteers host Sunday morning walks and feedings. Small pasture, not a formal attraction.

P.w: A 1912 Mediterranean-Revival villa built by Senator James Phelan, now an arts center set in 175 hillside acres with formal gardens, an outdoor amphitheater, an artist residency, and free hiking trails through the redwoods.
P.k: Grounds and trails open daily 8am-sunset, free parking on weekdays; villa interior access varies with events and tours.

P.ad: 106 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
P.w: A community art and history museum in downtown Los Gatos with rotating contemporary-art and local-history exhibitions, an easy stop on a day trip to the town's shops and the Los Gatos Creek Trail.
P.k: Closed Mon-Tue; open Wed-Sun. Free for Los Gatos residents and under-18s; modest admission otherwise.

P.ad: 201 S Market St, San Jose, CA 95113
P.w: A hands-on science and technology center in downtown San Jose with interactive innovation labs, a design workshop, and an IMAX dome theater, aimed at families and curious minds.
P.k: Since June 2026 on a reduced schedule; closed Mondays and Tuesdays. Not permanently closed despite some stale listings.

P.w: The sandstone Romanesque heart of Stanford's campus, where the arcaded Main Quad frames Memorial Church, famed for its gold-leaf mosaic facade and stained glass, built by Jane Stanford in memory of Leland.
P.k: Free and open to the public; the Quad is walkable any time and the church is open daily outside services. Docent tours Fridays.

P.n: Cantor Arts Center & Rodin Sculpture Garden
P.w: Stanford's free art museum spanning 5,000 years, holding the largest Rodin collection outside Paris - including a cast of The Gates of Hell - with an outdoor Rodin Sculpture Garden open around the clock.
P.k: Free admission; museum closed Tuesdays. The outdoor sculpture garden is open 24/7 and lit at night.

P.w: A jewel-box museum of postwar American modern and contemporary art - Pollock, Rothko, Diebenkorn, de Kooning - given to Stanford by the Anderson family, next door to the Cantor Arts Center.
P.k: Always free; open Thursday-Monday, closed Tuesday and Wednesday. No reservation needed.

P.w: Stanford's acoustically acclaimed 842-seat 'vineyard'-style concert hall, opened in 2013, where audience terraces wrap the stage so no seat sits more than 75 feet from the performers.
P.k: A performing-arts venue - visitable by attending a Stanford Live concert or event; check the calendar for public performances.

P.ad: 525 S Winchester Blvd, San Jose, CA 95128
P.w: The sprawling, labyrinthine Victorian mansion built continuously for decades by rifle heiress Sarah Winchester, riddled with stairs to nowhere, doors opening onto walls, and 160 rooms.
P.k: Guided tours only, by ticket; open daily. On the National Register of Historic Places.

P.w: The largest collection of Egyptian antiquities on display in western North America - mummies, sarcophagi, amulets, and a walk-in replica rock-cut tomb - set in a distinctive Egyptian-Revival campus.
P.k: Ticketed; check days open before visiting. Free parking at Naglee Ave and Chapman St, one block east.

P.ad: 500 El Camino Real, Santa Clara, CA 95053
P.w: The eighth of California's 21 Franciscan missions, founded in 1777 and now the centerpiece of Santa Clara University, with a restored adobe-style church, rose gardens, and centuries-old olive trees.
P.k: Free; grounds and church open daily roughly 7am-7pm. No guided tours (self-guided pamphlet available). Free visitor parking permit at the campus kiosk on weekdays.

P.ad: 80 S Market St, San Jose, CA 95113
P.w: San Jose's landmark downtown cathedral, an 1877 Italianate-Renaissance church crowned by a great dome, richly frescoed inside and designated a minor basilica by the Vatican.
P.k: Free to visit outside of Mass and services; open to the public in downtown San Jose.

P.w: A 14-acre open-air museum in Kelley Park with 30-plus original and re-created homes, shops, and landmarks of early San Jose - including a half-scale Electric Light Tower - plus a working trolley and the O'Brien's ice cream parlor.
P.k: Park grounds free to walk; some buildings and the trolley run on limited days. Run by History San Jose.

F.w: San Jose's cult Southern-style smokehouse and perennial local BBQ champ; go for the slow-smoked beef brisket with the house sauces, plus St. Louis ribs, pulled pork and the fried Louisiana Hots. The old Newhall Dr location closed; this 4th St spot is the one that's open.

Downtown flagship on San Carlos (the old 80 N Market location is closed; Capitol Expy and 13th St branches also open).

F.w: Cupertino's landmark high-end steakhouse and a California pioneer of imported Japanese wagyu; the draw is one of the region's deepest A5 wagyu selections plus dry-aged, hand-cut prime steaks with Japanese accents. Reopened end of July 2026 after a renovation.

F.w: The Palo Alto outpost of the cult Bay Area bubble-tea brand (founded in SF's Mission, 2011) that helped push American boba upscale — house-brewed organic teas, Straus Family Creamery milk and hand-cooked tapioca in the signature jasmine milk tea. Open (verified Aug 2026).

The Taiwanese bakery-cafe juggernaut whose Cupertino store draws constant trays-and-tongs crowds; the famous iced sea salt coffee (cold brew capped with a salty-sweet cream float) and the marble taro bread are the must-grabs. The Milpitas branch has closed; this one is open (verified Aug 2026).

F.ad: 19449 Stevens Creek Blvd Ste 120, Cupertino, CA 95014
F.w: A destination for authentic Taiwanese dessert (the chain began in Taichung, 1996); the signature is a warm bowl of hand-made Q-chewy taro balls over silky herbal grass jelly with red bean and taro. Open (verified Mar 2026).

The South Bay branch of the San Mateo-born chain (started by Alex Su out of a downtown San Mateo shop) that became a Bay Area boba phenomenon on the back of its honey boba and mix-and-match flavor wall. Open (verified Aug 2026).

F.w: Cupertino outpost of the Taiwanese brand TP Tea (茶湯會), from the founding family behind Chatime; the roasted tie guan yin milk tea crowned with salty cheese cream foam is the pick, with chewy house pearls. Open (verified Aug 2026).

F.w: A Silicon Valley-born boba brand (founded 2019 by local engineers) that leans on fresh-fruit teas and cheese-foam toppings; now several South Bay shops strong. Open (verified Jul 2026).
West San Jose shop of the Taiwanese chain Tea Top, a boba-scene staple for its brown sugar fresh milk with warm chewy pearls and jasmine milk tea. Open (verified Jul 2026).

F.ad: 2936 Aborn Square Rd, San Jose, CA 95121
F.w: A long-running Taiwanese-style boba spot on San Jose's east side known for a big roster of milk teas and slushes; the Okinawa and Hokkaido milk teas are the go-tos. Open (verified Aug 2026).

F.w: San Jose branch of the global Taiwanese chain Sharetea (est. 1992), a reliable pour for classic pearl milk tea and QQ (pearl + herbal jelly) toppings. Open (verified Apr 2026).

The iconic community cafe smack in the middle of downtown Mountain View's Castro Street — red walls, a laptop-packed upstairs loft, and a beloved Monday open-mic; a South Bay institution for founders, students and artists. Open (verified Jul 2026).

A geeky West San Jose specialty roaster that roasts single-origin beans in-store on a zero-emissions roaster and brews with mineral-tuned water — one of the Valley's most precise cups. Open (verified Aug 2026).

An indoor/outdoor French patisserie on Santana Row baking daily — croissants, tarts, cakes and a rainbow of macarons, plus baguette sandwiches; open late on weekends. Open (verified Aug 2026).
The Cupertino branch of the Bay Area's Taiwanese-style bakery chain near Apple Park; go for the soft milk breads, taro buns and coffee-cream loaves, plus milk tea to go. Open (verified Aug 2026).
